hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -10}h(x)$ represents the limit of $h$ as $x$ approaches $-10$.

Let's look at the table and see if the $h(x)$-values seem to approach a distinct finite value as the $x$-values approach $-10$.

$x$ | $-10.1$ | $-10.01$ | $-10.001$ 
:- | :-: | :-: | :-:  
$h(x)$ | $-9.89$ | $-9.47$ | $-9.02$ 

As the $x$-values *increase towards* $x=-10$ (i.e. approach it from the left), the $h(x)$-values seem to approach $-9$.

$x$ | $-9.999$ | $-9.99$ | $-9.9$
:- | :-: | :-: | :-: 
$h(x)$ | $-8.01$ | $-8.3$ | $-8.94$

As the $x$-values *decrease towards* $x=-10$ (i.e. approach it from the right), the $h(x)$-values seem to approach $-8$.
The function doesn't seem to approach the same value from both sides, so the limit doesn't exist.

question.content:
The function $h$ is defined over the real numbers. This table gives a few values of $h$.

$x$ | $-10.1$ | $-10.01$ | $-10.001$ | $-9.999$ | $-9.99$ | $-9.9$
:- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: 
$h(x)$ | $-9.89$ | $-9.47$ | $-9.02$ | $-8.01$ | $-8.3$ | $-8.94$

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -10}h(x)$?**
